learn.title: Size and direction
learn.body: A vector is an arrow. Its length is the magnitude and its angle is the direction. Speed is just a number, but a velocity of 10 m/s at $30^\circ$ is a vector. We write a vector by its steps, such as $(3,4)$: 3 right, 4 up.

learn.title: Magnitude and angle
learn.body: The magnitude of $(x,y)$ is $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$. The angle from the positive $x$-axis comes from $\tan^{-1}\frac{y}{x}$, adjusted for the quadrant. Going the other way: $x=r\cos\theta$ and $y=r\sin\theta$.

learn.title: Adding and scaling
learn.body: Add vectors component by component, which is the same as placing arrows tip to tail: $(3,4)+(1,-2)=(4,2)$. Scaling multiplies each part: $2(3,4)=(6,8)$ is twice as long, in the same direction.

questions.prompt: What is the magnitude of the vector $(3,4)$?

questions.explanation: Add the first parts and add the second parts.

questions.prompt: A force of 20 acts at $120^\circ$. What is its $x$-component? Give a number.
The vector $(3,4)$ points at about what angle?
Adding vectors by placing arrows is called \_\_ addition.
questions.explanation: Put the start of the second arrow at the end of the first.

questions.prompt: Match each idea to its formula.
questions.explanation: Components come from a right triangle.

questions.prompt: Two vectors have the same magnitude but different directions. Are they equal?
choices: No, equal vectors need the same size and direction
questions.explanation: A vector is defined by both.
